text:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT PAGE: Potential cross-tenant egress detected from dedicated pool dp-08 affecting customer-b-2119. Trigger: routemgr anomaly detector. Severity: P2 -> paging on-call. Auto-collect: packet captures started. Paging: @emily_r @raj_patel @jordan_lee

emily_r: Picking this up. Oncall here. Any immediate customer impact noted?

raj_patel: Quick heads-up — I'm remote but can help with rules and iptables. If this is route-table duplication, we may need a hotfix.

jordan_lee: Initial findings: multiple src-tenants showing next-hop towards tenant-cidr 10.200.21.0/24 which belongs to tenant 2119, but packets originate from pods in dp-08 bound to tenant 718. Possible prefix shadowing in route table. Snippets below from node-14: 
```
$ sudo ip route show table all | grep 10.200.21
10.200.21.0/24 via 172.31.14.7 dev eth0 proto static metric 100 pref 0
10.200.0.0/16 via 172.31.9.2 dev eth0 proto static metric 200 pref 0
```
Observing simultaneous entries with different metrics. Also tcpdump shows SYNs to customer endpoints with X-Tenant header set to 718.
```
15:42:18.432123 IP 10.42.3.21.33524 > 10.200.21.45.443: Flags [S], seq 1234567, win 64240
HTTP: X-Tenant: 718
```

emily_r: Thanks Jordan. Sec note: preserve captures. @sec_ops can you confirm retention and copy location?

sec_ops: Confirmed. Grabbing pcap from node-14 now and pushing to forensic bucket. Command I'm running: 
```
ssh root@node-14 'tcpdump -i any -w /var/log/pcap/dp08-suspect.pcap host 10.200.21.45'
scp root@node-14:/var/log/pcap/dp08-suspect.pcap sec-forensic@storage:/pcaps/1960009999-dp08.pcap
```
Also snapshotting kernel route tables and iptables.

maria_g: FYI customer-b-2119 is an enterprise VPC customer, security team wants immediate notification if PII could be exposed. I'm opening a bridge and pinging their SE.

emily_r: Immediate mitigation plan: 1) Block egress from dp-08 to 10.200.21.0/24 2) Enable strict tenant-binding on routemgr for dp-08 3) Preserve artifacts. Executing step 1 now via routemgr tool.

emily_r: Running: 
```
./routemgr block --pool dp-08 --cidr 10.200.21.0/24 --reason "egress-misroute-1960009999" --temp 3600
```

oncall-bot: Action logged: routemgr block executed by emily_r at 1960009805.

jordan_lee: After block, no new outbound connections seen to that prefix from dp-08. Netstat snapshot: 
```
$ netstat -anp | grep 10.200.21
(no active sessions)
```

raj_patel: Good. Next: root cause triage. My hunch: control plane pushed a stale prefix from legacy config service during a recent deployment. Let's check config-sync service for dp-08's last config update.

eng-runtime: Pulling config change history for dp-08 now. Found a merge at 1960009600 from deploy pipeline which added a catch-all 10.200.0.0/16 entry without tenant metadata. This likely created a less-specific route that took precedence for some flows. Stack: routemgr builds kernel routes from config-sync.

eng-runtime: Proposed immediate hotfix: prefer route entries with tenant-binding flag when multiple prefixes overlap. Pushing a canary to route reconciler: setting prefer_tenant_binding=true for dp-08. Deploying to reconciler canary group 3.

maria_g: Customer comms: I'll draft a short message for SE: "We detected and mitigated a routing anomaly that briefly allowed dp-08 traffic toward a prefix owned by tenant 2119. We blocked the path, preserved packet captures, and are doing a root-cause fix. We'll follow up with timeline and impact assessment." Anyone want to add?

emily_r: Add that we have no confirmed exfil of payloads beyond SYN/establish attempts recorded. We will confirm after pcap analysis.

sec_ops: Pcap shows only initial TLS handshakes, no authenticated requests with user payload. Parsing full pcaps now but so far looks like connection attempts. Saving extracted metadata to incident bucket.

oncall-bot: Incident status update: severity remains P2. Mitigation applied (egress block). Artifacts collected: /pcaps/1960009999-dp08.pcap, /snapshots/node-14-routes-1960009999.txt.

raj_patel: After canary looks good, we should rollout tenant-binding hotfix globally and backfill a validation test into the config pipeline to reject catch-all prefixes without tenant metadata. I can own the pipeline test.

emily_r: Agreed. Immediate next steps: 1) Confirm pcap analysis (sec_ops) 2) Validate canary for 15 minutes (eng-runtime) 3) Notify customer SE (maria_g) 4) Create post-incident ticket for config pipeline fix (raj_patel). I'll stay on this until handoff to eng-runtime and sec_ops for follow-up.

maria_g: Bridge created: https://meet.redwood.internal/incident-1960009999. SE brief scheduled in 20m.

eng-runtime: Canary completed at 1960010120 with no regressions; route reconciler now prefers tenant-binding on dp-08. Scheduling global rollout with 5-min ramp.

sec_ops: Pcap analysis done: no payloads containing cleartext PII observed; metadata indicates only TLS handshake attempts and resets. We'll attach full report to the ticket.

emily_r: Handoff: I'll mark incident as mitigated in the pager and handoff to eng-runtime for permanent fix and raj_patel for pipeline test. Please update the incident tracker with links to artifacts.

oncall-bot: Incident mitigated by emily_r at 1960010305. Severity: P2 -> mitigated. Next owner(s): eng-runtime (permanent fix), raj_patel (pipeline test), sec_ops (forensic report).

maria_g: I'll send the customer update: short summary + timeline + "we found no evidence of PII exfiltration" per sec_ops preliminary.

emily_r: Thanks team. Follow-ups: ticket INC-1960009999 created for full RCA, ETA 48h. Closing this Slack thread but keep monitoring dashboards for 24h. :thumbsup: :eyes:
